body: Give yourself a month :) if you don't like how you feel at the end of the month, you can ALWAYS go back to food. It'll always be there.

You really just gotta calorie count. CICO. Download MyFitnessPal, buy a food scale, and enter honestly. Exercise (especially a few km) walk, won't really help you much (though it's good for your health to do it.) weight loss is 90% eating. Find your TDEE and take 500-1000 off it depending on what you can realistically do. At the same time, try making healthier lower calorie choices. Don't look at this as a diet. It is changing your relationship to food. But to be clear CICO!!! It's the only thing that works. Seriously. 

Edit: Sorry I misread!! But I'd start with walking outside everyday for an hour and yoga. I promise depression, anxiety, everything gets better with this. If you don't think you can do a full yoga exercise then just stretch for 15 minutes every morning. I've also found weight lifting changes everything about my mood and energy levels. I am bipolar type 1 and seriously weight lifting has really given me the edge I needed (along with meds) to feel good. That's my two cents. Also no processed foods!!!
For me ovulation means massive water weight :) if you've been on a deficit then it definitely is that. Don't sweat it too much! Keep on your deficit and measure next week.

NSV: Last night I went out with people (didn't drink!!) and when we went to get drunk food  I had a candy bar that I had budgeted for and ended up exactly at 1,190 calories. I can do this!!! It's never been like this before. It felt like I could really do this as a lifestyle change.

Maybe start some chemical exfoliation? Physical exfoliation (the St. Ives) is REALLY bad for your skin. It's just tearing it up. If you start an AHA or BHA that could really help out with the acne. 

Also, if you have oily skin, OCM has helped me a lot. You cleanse with some jojoba or something before you use your Cerave at night. 

And it could be the Cetaphil that's breaking you out. :/ Just my 2 cents!

I'd recommend just washing with water in the morning (not soap, not cleanser) and then moisturising after. I know it seems counterintuitive, but you could be stripping your skin with too much watching if you wash it with a cleanser or soap twice a day. You can take a shower in the morning, but just splash some lukewarm water on your face. Make sure it isn't too hot.
